cases.title: Running DG: Import shared nodes opens a dialog titled Import shared nodes

cases.proves: Done When 8: Change the dialog title and entry points labeled "Discover shared nodes" to "Import shared nodes"
cases.checks: The dialog's title is Import shared nodes, and nothing in it says Discover shared nodes.
cases.caption: The command and the dialog are now called Import shared nodes.

expect.js: proof.waitFor(() => { const dialog = proof.dialogs()[0]; const title = dialog && dialog.querySelector('.bp3-dialog-header'); return Boolean(title) && title.innerText.trim() === 'Import shared nodes' && !proof.dialogText().includes('Discover shared nodes'); }, { what: 'a dialog titled Import shared nodes' })

cases.title: The import table shows only the Source space, Title and Modified columns
cases.proves: Done When 2: The status, source node ID, and "Source app" columns are removed.
cases.checks: The column headers are exactly Source space, Title and Modified.
cases.caption: Status, source node ID and Source app are gone. Source space, Title and Modified are left.

expect.js: (() => { const heads = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-dialog thead th')).map((cell) => cell.innerText.trim()).filter(Boolean); proof.assert(JSON.stringify(heads) === JSON.stringify(['Source space', 'Title', 'Modified']), 'The columns are ' + JSON.stringify(heads)); const text = proof.dialogText(); proof.assert(!/Status|Source app|Source node ID|Source ID/.test(text), 'A removed column is still on screen.'); })()

cases.title: The import table opens sorted by Modified, newest first
cases.proves: Done When 3: Users can sort the table by its data columns. The default order is last modified, most recent first.
cases.checks: The nodes run from the newest Modified time to the oldest, and Modified shows the sort arrow.
cases.caption: With no click, the newest node is first and the oldest is last.

expect.js: (() => { const rows = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-dialog tbody tr')).filter((row) => /Daylight exposure|Caffeine after noon|Cool bedrooms|Light therapy/.test(row.innerText)); proof.assert(rows.length === 4, 'Expected the four published nodes, found ' + rows.length); const times = rows.map((row) => Date.parse(row.querySelector('td[title]').getAttribute('title'))); proof.assert(new Set(times).size === 4, 'The modified times are not all different.'); proof.assert(times.every((time, index) => index === 0 || times[index - 1] > time), 'The rows are not newest first.'); proof.assert(rows[0].innerText.includes('Light therapy lifts winter mood'), 'The newest node is not first.'); proof.assert(Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-dialog th')).find((cell) => cell.innerText.trim() === 'Modified').getAttribute('aria-sort') === 'descending', 'Modified is not the sorted column.'); })()

cases.title: Clicking Title sorts Z to A, and clicking it again sorts A to Z

do.js: window.__titlesAfterFirstClick = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-dialog tbody tr')).filter((row) => /Daylight exposure|Caffeine after noon|Cool bedrooms|Light therapy/.test(row.innerText)).map((row) => row.querySelectorAll('td')[2].innerText.trim()); window.__sortAfterFirstClick = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-dialog th')).find((cell) => cell.innerText.trim() === 'Title').getAttribute('aria-sort')

cases.proves: Done When 5, 6 and 7: on click sort descending, on click against ascending; see relations as example
cases.checks: After one click the titles run Z to A. After the second they run A to Z.
cases.caption: First click on Title sorts Z to A, the next one A to Z.

expect.js: (() => { const compare = (a, b) => a.localeCompare(b, undefined, { numeric: true, sensitivity: 'base' }); const first = window.__titlesAfterFirstClick; proof.assert(window.__sortAfterFirstClick === 'descending', 'The first click gave ' + window.__sortAfterFirstClick); proof.assert(first.length === 4 && first.every((title, index) => index === 0 || compare(first[index - 1], title) >= 0), 'The first click did not sort Z to A: ' + JSON.stringify(first)); const second = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-dialog tbody tr')).filter((row) => /Daylight exposure|Caffeine after noon|Cool bedrooms|Light therapy/.test(row.innerText)).map((row) => row.querySelectorAll('td')[2].innerText.trim()); proof.assert(Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-dialog th')).find((cell) => cell.innerText.trim() === 'Title').getAttribute('aria-sort') === 'ascending', 'The second click did not give ascending.'); proof.assert(second.every((title, index) => index === 0 || compare(second[index - 1], title) <= 0), 'The second click did not sort A to Z: ' + JSON.stringify(second)); })()

cases.intent: Click Title once, then again. Click Source space, then Modified. Use titles with numbers like 'Claim 9' and 'Claim 10' and mixed case.

expect.js: (() => { const compare = (a, b) => a.localeCompare(b, undefined, { numeric: true, sensitivity: 'base' }); const snaps = window.__sortSnaps; proof.assert(snaps.length === 5, 'Expected five snapshots, got ' + snaps.length); snaps.forEach((snap) => proof.assert(snap.titles.length === 4, 'Expected the four sort-test nodes, got ' + JSON.stringify(snap.titles))); const s = snaps; proof.assert(s[0].sorted.join() === 'Source space:descending' && s[0].spaces.every((name, i) => i === 0 || compare(s[0].spaces[i - 1], name) >= 0), 'Source space first click: ' + JSON.stringify(s[0])); proof.assert(new Set(s[0].spaces).size === 2, 'Expected two source spaces: ' + JSON.stringify(s[0].spaces)); proof.assert(s[1].sorted.join() === 'Source space:ascending' && s[1].spaces.every((name, i) => i === 0 || compare(s[1].spaces[i - 1], name) <= 0), 'Source space second click: ' + JSON.stringify(s[1])); proof.assert(s[2].sorted.join() === 'Title:descending' && JSON.stringify(s[2].titles) === JSON.stringify(['PKS - Claim 10', 'PKS - Claim 9', 'PKS - claim 2', 'PKS - Claim 1']), 'Title descending: ' + JSON.stringify(s[2].titles)); proof.assert(s[3].sorted.join() === 'Title:ascending' && JSON.stringify(s[3].titles) === JSON.stringify(['PKS - Claim 1', 'PKS - claim 2', 'PKS - Claim 9', 'PKS - Claim 10']), 'Title ascending: ' + JSON.stringify(s[3].titles)); proof.assert(s[4].sorted.join() === 'Modified:descending' && s[4].times.every((time, i) => i === 0 || s[4].times[i - 1] > time), 'Modified: ' + JSON.stringify(s[4])); })()

cases.caption: Source space, Title and Modified each sort descending on the first click and ascending on the second. Claim 9 sorts before Claim 10, whatever the case.
cases.checks: Each click orders the four PKS nodes by the clicked column in the direction it asks for, with numbers in order and case ignored: Claim 1, claim 2, Claim 9, Claim 10. Modified ends newest first.

cases.title: The dialog keeps its height, and the search field, column headers and footer stay in view while the rows scroll

do.js: window.__dialogHeights = [Math.round(document.querySelector('.bp3-dialog').getBoundingClientRect().height)]

steps.why: Scroll the table to its last row

do.js: (() => { const table = document.querySelector('.bp3-dialog table'); let box = table.parentElement; while (box && !box.classList.contains('bp3-dialog') && !(box.scrollHeight > box.clientHeight + 1 && /auto|scroll/.test(getComputedStyle(box).overflowY))) box = box.parentElement; proof.assert(box && !box.classList.contains('bp3-dialog'), 'Nothing in the dialog scrolls the rows.'); box.scrollTop = box.scrollHeight; })()

steps.why: Note where the search field, column headers, last row and footer sit

do.js: (() => { const dialog = document.querySelector('.bp3-dialog'); const box = (element) => element.getBoundingClientRect(); const footer = dialog.querySelector('.bp3-dialog-footer'); const buttons = Array.from(footer.querySelectorAll('button')); const close = buttons.find((button) => button.innerText.trim() === 'Close'); const importButton = buttons.find((button) => button.innerText.includes('Import selected')); const count = footer.querySelector('span'); window.__dialogLayout = { bodyTop: box(dialog.querySelector('.bp3-dialog-body')).top, searchTop: box(dialog.querySelector('input[placeholder="Search shared nodes"]')).top, searchBottom: box(dialog.querySelector('input[placeholder="Search shared nodes"]')).bottom, columnsTop: box(dialog.querySelector('thead')).top, columnsBottom: box(dialog.querySelector('thead')).bottom, lastRowBottom: box(dialog.querySelector('tbody tr:last-child')).bottom, footerTop: box(footer).top, footerRight: box(footer).right, countRight: box(count).right, closeLeft: box(close).left, importRight: box(importButton).right }; })()

cases.proves: Done When 9: The dialog keeps a fixed height as its contents change. Its contents scroll while the header and footer remain visible.
cases.checks: The dialog is the same height with a full table and an empty one. With the rows scrolled to the end, the search field and the column headers show in full at the top of the dialog body, the last row sits above the footer, and the footer has the node count on the left and the buttons on the right.
cases.caption: The dialog stays the same height when the list empties out. The title and the buttons stay in view.

expect.js: (() => { const heights = window.__dialogHeights; proof.assert(heights.length === 2 && heights[0] === heights[1], 'The dialog height changed: ' + JSON.stringify(heights)); proof.assert(heights[0] <= window.innerHeight, 'The dialog is taller than the window.'); const layout = window.__dialogLayout; const at = ' ' + JSON.stringify(layout); proof.assert(layout.searchTop >= layout.bodyTop - 1, 'The search field is cut off at the top of the dialog body.' + at); proof.assert(layout.columnsTop >= layout.searchBottom - 1, 'The column headers scrolled out of view.' + at); proof.assert(layout.lastRowBottom <= layout.footerTop + 1, 'The last row is hidden behind the footer.' + at); proof.assert(layout.importRight >= layout.footerRight - 2, 'Import selected is not at the right of the footer.' + at); proof.assert(layout.closeLeft - layout.countRight > 40, 'The buttons sit next to the node count instead of on the right.' + at); })()

cases.proves: Done When 10: After import, clicking an imported-node link in the result opens the imported node in Roam.
cases.caption: Import two shared claims. The result now lists each imported node as a link, not only the ones with warnings.

expect.js: (async () => { const callout = await proof.waitFor(() => { const found = proof.byText('.bp3-dialog .bp3-callout', 'imported'); if (!found) return false; const texts = Array.from(found.querySelectorAll('li a')).map((link) => link.innerText); return found.innerText.includes('2 imported') && texts.some((text) => text.includes('Daylight exposure')) && texts.some((text) => text.includes('Caffeine after noon')) && found; }, { what: 'a result listing both imported claims as links', timeout: 20000 }); proof.assert(callout.scrollHeight <= callout.clientHeight + 1, 'The result is squeezed: it shows ' + callout.clientHeight + 'px of its ' + callout.scrollHeight + 'px.'); const body = document.querySelector('.bp3-dialog .bp3-dialog-body').getBoundingClientRect(); const search = document.querySelector('.bp3-dialog input[placeholder="Search shared nodes"]').getBoundingClientRect(); proof.assert(search.top >= body.top - 1 && search.height >= 20, 'The search field is cut off once the result shows.'); })()

cases.checks: The result counts 2 imported and lists both claims as links. The result shows in full, and the search field above it isn't cut off.

cases.title: Import progress and the result show in the same place, above the table

steps.why: Start watching for the progress bar

do.js: (() => { window.__progressSeen = null; window.__progressWatch && window.__progressWatch.disconnect(); window.__progressWatch = new MutationObserver(() => { const callout = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-dialog .bp3-callout')).find((item) => item.innerText.trim().startsWith('Importing')); if (callout && !window.__progressSeen) window.__progressSeen = { parent: callout.parentElement, index: Array.from(callout.parentElement.children).indexOf(callout), top: Math.round(callout.getBoundingClientRect().top) }; }); window.__progressWatch.observe(document.body, { childList: true, subtree: true }); })()

expect.js: (() => { const seen = window.__progressSeen; window.__progressWatch && window.__progressWatch.disconnect(); proof.assert(seen, 'No progress callout was shown during the import.'); const result = proof.byText('.bp3-dialog .bp3-callout', '1 imported'); proof.assert(result, 'No result callout.'); proof.assert(result.parentElement === seen.parent, 'The result is in a different container than the progress.'); proof.assert(Array.from(result.parentElement.children).indexOf(result) === seen.index, 'The result is at a different position than the progress.'); proof.assert(Math.abs(Math.round(result.getBoundingClientRect().top) - seen.top) <= 2, 'The result is at a different height than the progress.'); })()

expect.js: (() => { const callout = proof.byText('.bp3-dialog .bp3-callout', '1 failed'); proof.assert(callout, 'No result callout.'); proof.assert(callout.querySelector('.bp3-heading').innerText.trim() === '1 imported, 0 skipped, 1 failed, 1 with warnings', 'The title is ' + callout.querySelector('.bp3-heading').innerText.trim()); proof.assert(callout.classList.contains('bp3-intent-warning'), 'The callout is not a warning.'); const items = Array.from(callout.querySelectorAll('li')); const failed = items.find((item) => item.innerText.includes('Collision claim')); proof.assert(failed && !failed.querySelector('a') && failed.innerText.includes('already exists'), 'The failed claim is not listed with its reason: ' + (failed && failed.innerText)); const warned = items.find((item) => item.querySelector('a') && item.querySelector('a').innerText.trim() === 'PKE - Cold showers raise alertness - [[@placeholder]]'); proof.assert(warned && warned.innerText.includes('No source was published with this node.'), 'The warned node is not listed as a link with its warning.'); proof.assert(proof.byText('.bp3-dialog tbody tr', 'Collision claim'), 'The failed claim left the table.'); proof.assert(proof.byText('.bp3-dialog button', 'Import selected (1)'), 'The failed claim is not still selected.'); })()

title: Simplify the Roam import dialog and import feedback
